overview: This Senate resolution honors former First Lady Barbara Bush on what would have been her 100th birthday, June 8, 2025. It reviews her life, including her marriage to President George H. W. Bush, raising six children, and her roles as Second Lady and First Lady. It highlights her work promoting reading and literacy, including founding the Barbara Bush Foundation for Family Literacy and supporting the National Literacy Act of 1991, and her compassion toward AIDS patients. It notes she was the second woman in U.S. history to be both the wife and mother of a president, and that she died in 2018. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 17, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution fittingly honors a First Lady whose literacy work had a lasting effect on families across the country.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
